title: The Blood of Dawnwalker
description:
Bringing together a talented team of developers, including members of the core team behind one of the most acclaimed games of all time - The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt along with its expansions, Rebel Wolves’ first title is a dark fantasy narrative sandbox, AAA action-RPG set in medieval Europe.

This brand-new IP is aimed at mature audiences and is powered by Unreal Engine 5.

critic_reviews.quote: The Blood of Dawnwalker is one of the most impressive games I’ve played this generation. The sprawling world and multifaceted story are wonders to behold, while the combat walks the perfect line between complexity and accessibility. Though there is a little bit of open-world jank to contend with, you’d be missing out by choosing not to play this game, as it may already be the best release in an extremely competitive September.

Rebel Wolves may have built the game on familiar open-world RPG foundations, but The Blood of Dawnwalker ultimately establishes an identity entirely its own. Its ambitious storytelling, rewarding combat and excellent vampire mechanics make it a genuine Game of the Year contender, and an absolute must-play for RPG fans.

Ultimately, I loved exploring the world Rebel Wolves has built with The Blood of Dawn Walker. While Coen and his companions often feel a bit too young and beautiful for the gritty story they inhabit, Vale Sangora feels rich within the limits of its mountain range. The directional combat was a lovely change from simple three-button combos and a pleasure to master, while the time resource management mechanic helped me maintain focus without feeling overly pressured. If you have ever enjoyed Skyrim, The Witcher, or a Red Dead game, I suspect there is a lot here you will love. My family will soon be complaining that I’m busy saving Coen’s family too often as I run through multiple playthroughs over the coming weeks.

Simply exploring the world counts as a free action for those who just want to see what’s around and discover what they can find, while finding secrets and transforming your Coen as a result is an engaging blast. The scenario writing and character work deliver on all the expectations from The Witcher 3, with plenty of morally tricky propositions for the player to uncover and crack. It’s the sort of game that you want to revisit as soon as you set it down. Strong graphics, great storytelling, and solid gameplay all come together to deliver one of the best games of the year. If you like games like The Witcher 3 or Elden Ring, Blood of the Dawnwalker is a must-play experience. Even if you don’t like those games, the strength of the execution in Rebel Wolves’ first game is worth checking out and admiring.

Supported by sharp combat, deep day-night synergy, a fantastic score, and a lived-in world, the game delivers on its ambitious promises. Minor hiccups like stiff facial animations or initial calendar anxiety do nothing to diminish what Rebel Wolves has achieved here. The Blood of Dawnwalker isn't just an outstanding RPG; it is a landmark statement in game design that proves restraint, atmosphere, and meaningful player agency beat mindless scale every single time. An absolute, brilliantly executed dark fantasy masterpiece.

Most Western RPGs have been overshadowed this year by an incredible run of JRPGs, both those already released and several more looming on the horizon in the coming months. Against that backdrop, The Blood of Dawnwalker might genuinely be one of the best games 2026 has to offer. It has it all and then some, constantly surprising with consummate professionalism and polish.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a game that lays its ambitions bare at the beginning, and one-by-one pays off all those ambitions in remarkable ways. It’s a game that grips you early on, and sinks its teeth into you more with every passing hour.

The Blood of Dawnwalker understands something that most open-world RPGs seem to forget. You cannot experience everything. Time is always moving forward, and how you spend it is important. Having to make those sacrifices initially frustrated me because I wanted to see everything the game had to offer, but eventually it became the reason I enjoyed the journey so much. It also makes The Blood of Dawnwalker highly replayable, because there will always be things you left behind to discover on another playthrough. And with that, I am off to play it all again.

The Blood of Dawnwalker does almost everything right that you'd expect from an action role-playing game. Exceptional gameplay, a story full of twists and turns, and an immersive gaming experience make Rebel Wolves' debut a contender for Game of the Year.
The Blood of Dawnwalker is a fantastic RPG worthy of diving and sinking your fangs into again and again.

The game goes a step beyond merely being a homage, and perhaps borrows a few too many gameplay elements from the legendary The Witcher 3, but it's hard not to be quite considerably impressed by what Rebel Wolves has achieved here. The Blood of Dawnwalker offers innovative solutions to well-established design challenges that far larger, more experienced studios have been unable to resolve, and it does so with flair, character, and enthusiasm.

Ladies and gentlemen, without mincing words or beating around the bush, The Blood of Dawnwalker is simply a great video game. Rebel Wolves hits the mark perfectly and delivers a debut that confidently enters the club of the best action RPGs on the market. Never predictable and capable of breathing new life — or rather, new blood — into the vampire mythos, The Blood of Dawnwalker offers adrenaline-fueled combat, deep and customizable character progression, solid technical performance, and an interesting story capable of engaging the player, also thanks to the possibility of making choices that have a real impact on events. Sure, some elements could have used a little more polish, and some mechanics can feel cumbersome, but that doesn't change the fact that Coen's adventures will entertain you and keep you glued to your controller. The Blood of Dawnwalker is one of the biggest and most interesting surprises the 2026 gaming year could have given us.

The Blood of Dawnwalker deserves to be a new AAA mainstay, and I’d gladly join Coen on future ventures. Rebel Wolves’ debut outing is everything you could want from the former director of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, but it’s also something entirely new. Its time mechanic is risky - and a nightmare for completionists - but it adds a brilliant sense of urgency into the open-world. The Blood of Dawnwalker is all about consequence. Which quests should you tackle? As a human or a vampire? It’s entirely what you make of it, offering up a bold and engaging formula that I’d be glad to see walk away with 2026’s GOTY trophy.

The Blood of Dawnwalker has a familiar DNA, yet manages to carve out a distinct identity as an RPG. Its time-based system forces players to carefully consider their next move, giving greater weight to every decision they make. Strong writing, engaging combat, and rewarding exploration showcase the expertise its developers have refined over the years, resulting in a compelling and confidently crafted role-playing experience.
The Blood of Dawnwalker is an excellent open-world fantasy RPG with some unique, interesting ideas.
The Blood of Dawnwalker is an impressive, bloody cocktail of interesting ideas and well-written characters, making it one of this year’s best open-world RPGs.
The Blood of Dawnwalker is a fascinating action-RPG, where every choice to save Coen’s family feels rightly consequential.
The Blood of Dawnwalker is an excellent, albeit imperfect, starting point, but one that Rebel Wolves has used to forge its own path. If you love decision-making RPGs, you won't be disappointed.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is going to be one of the most memorable RPG experiences of the year. Not because it has a movie-like budget, but because it executes its ideas brilliantly and makes the most of what it has

Rest assured: The Blood of Dawnwalker is more than just "The Witcher with vampires." Rebel Wolves weave together proven action-RPG staples with an incredibly organic time-management mechanic and engaging, hybrid day-night gameplay. The result is a genuine RPG-gem; while it still has some technical kinks to iron out, in terms of both gameplay and narrative, it need not shy away from the genre’s heavyweights. I can hardly wait for a sequel already.
Blood of Dawnwalker features a great setting, a brilliant dual gameplay loop, and satisfying combat in a world I want to see much more of.

The Blood of Dawnwalker from developer Rebel Wolves is a great starting point for what could become a bigger series. It delivers a strong story, entertaining gameplay elements, and plenty of quests to keep the journey going.

Blood of Dawnwalker is much more than just another Witcher-like RPG. Its dark vampire setting, meaningful choices and strong storytelling give the game its own identity. The combat is challenging but flexible, while the time system and the differences between day and night add welcome depth. Some issues with controls, camera work and technical polish remain, but they rarely overshadow the overall experience. In short, Blood of Dawnwalker is one of the first major RPG highlights of the second half of 2026.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a fantastic open world RPG with a sharply written story, great characters and meaningful choices throughout. It wears its Witcher 3 inspirations on its sleeve, but isn't afraid to add some twists to keep it fresh.
A gripping vampire-RPG with tough choices, strong dialogue, and a cool parry system, but a formulaic open world.

In a month packed with big-name releases, The Blood of Dawnwalker might be one of the best games of the bunch. It's a well-crafted adventure with an engaging story, an enjoyable world, interesting powers and a genuinely compelling approach to player choice. The time limit gives every decision weight. The open-ended storytelling makes exploration meaningful. The day/night system gives Coen two distinct ways to interact with the world. Most importantly, the game trusts you to make choices without constantly telling you whether you've made the "right" one.

While it suffers from rough graphics and repetitive combat, The Blood of Dawnwalker delivers a deeply engaging narrative shaped by meaningful choices under a 30-day time limit. Driven by compelling characters and solid storytelling, it stands out as a rare gem among story-driven medieval RPGs.

The Blood of Dawnwalker manages to avoid becoming a mere repetition of familiar formulas and finds an identity of its own, thanks to a combination of reactive storytelling, meaningful exploration, and a time mechanic that alters how every decision is approached.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is more than an outstanding debut IP for Rebel Wolves. It comes with its own very well-executed ideas, a decision system with tangible consequences, and one of the most satisfying combat systems in the genre. It is not a 'The Witcher with vampires'; it is an adventure with its own personality that fans of action RPGs and medieval fantasy will love.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is an ambitious RPG that manages to step out of The Witcher 3’s shadow thanks to its clever use of time, meaningful choices, and the duality between human and vampire. On PS5, Quality Mode delivers impressive visuals while maintaining a solid 30 FPS, backed by excellent audio and a narrative structure where choices and their consequences genuinely matter.

Although it has some flaws in combat, The Blood of Dawnwalker delivers a solid and characterful experience. Its time management system, the freedom to explore, and the choices that shape Coen's journey are its greatest strengths and make Rebel Wolves' RPG stand out from other games in the genre.

The Blood of Dawnwalker bears all the hallmarks of a project crafted by brilliance, particularly through its top-tier storytelling and tight combat mechanics. Yet while its core identity as an Action RPG is rock-solid, the surrounding package lacks the high-end production polish needed to elevate it further. It’s an undeniable achievement, but one constantly shadowed by the obvious strain of a limited budget and workforce.

The Blood of the Dawnwalker is an impressive debut from Rebel Wolves, with challenging combat and choices that shape the story around you. It breathes life back into a tired genre of vampire action RPGs, using time as a resource and allowing the player to shape the world around them. Despite relatively benign issues that can easily be rectified, it is certainly one to watch within the world of RPGs.
The Blood of Dawnwalker impresses with its world-building, characters, and time-driven choices. Despite dated visuals, it’s an ambitious and compelling RPG debut.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is an ambitious, choice-driven vampire RPG with an intricately connected world, satisfying directional combat, and meaningful player agency throughout most of its journey. Repetitive enemies, technical issues, and a surprisingly rigid finale keep Rebel Wolves’ debut from reaching its full potential, but its compelling characters and nonlinear storytelling make it a promising start to a new RPG universe.
An original, macabre horror story with a strong setting, central narrative, and characters, though Coen is no Geralt.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is excellent, if not quite successful in everything it tries. It's fun to teleport around in a cloud of smoke and bats or walk on ceilings, but the story is also fantastic. It's probably even darker and grimmer than you're expecting, and it gripped me throughout and was complimented by equally fascinating side quest stories that I had to choose between. If you like RPGs, vampires, or great stories, you won't want to miss The Blood of Dawnwalker.
The Blood of Dawnwalker is a fantastic first outing from Rebel Wolves and the clear start of a franchise. It's full of smart ideas that have the making of another classic RPG franchise.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is both what was expected and what was feared: an RPG anchored in familiar structural mechanics that attempts to break new ground with a couple of fresh design ideas. The signature style of Rebel Wolves—a team largely hailing from CD Projekt Red—is most evident in the writing; the world-building, lore, and plot are compelling and satisfying, keeping players glued to their controllers for hours. Centered on Coen, the game features a "sandbox" spirit and a 30-day mechanic—two gambles that pay off in terms of replayability and a sense of consequence, even if the promised freedom is only partially realized. The result is an enjoyable debut that is magnetic at times, yet suffers from the flaws typical of a first outing.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a solid RPG with an intriguing time-based system and a compelling story filled with memorable characters and numerous paths to explore. However, issues with its combat and technical performance prevent it from fully realizing its ambitious vision. Even so, it remains a highly entertaining and worthwhile experience that is easy to recommend.

The narrative might be subservient to the mechanics, and not as thematically evocative as I might like, but excellent writing does combine with quality, well-executed mechanics to give us the equivalent of a pulp fantasy page-turner, and like the stories of dark pulp fantasy writer, Robert E. Howard, it’s really (really) difficult to put down.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a flawed game, but the heart at the centre of it is strong. Rebel Wolves certainly has work to do in this post-release period with balance, performance, and quality-of-life updates – but once this work is done, I feel this will be the first entry in what becomes a beloved saga. For all its faults, The Blood of Dawnwalker has sold me on its world and characters, and I am eager to take up my sword as Coen in the future.

Overall, The Blood of Dawnwalker is an incredibly ambitious, deeply interesting first game from Rebel Wolves. Not every good idea lands and not every envelope is pushed as far as it could be, but the potential of the game is vast, and there’s a huge amount to lean into and love. And it’s all bolstered by excellent writing that makes for one of the deepest and most interesting game worlds I’ve run across in some time. The Blood of Dawnwalker is the kind of RPG that feels great to get lost in, that digs into your mind and stays there, and which is worth scouring and savoring.

A stellar opening bite from Rebel Wolves, The Blood of Dawnwalker demonstrates it can claw and battle with the toughest of the vrakhir. While it's not quite at the level of the very best in the genre, it delivers a superb open world adventure, filled with intrigue and compelling combat. Give it enough time to feed and this Dawnwalker could grow into a titan, and I can't wait to see what blood feast will come next.

There’s plenty to do in The Blood of Dawnwalker, and I’ve already spent a great deal of time wondering how different decisions might have shaped the outcomes, enough so that I will be playing through it again straight away. For a game I wasn’t entirely sure about at first, I’m happy to be walking away with a new addition to my lineup of favorite RPGs, and one that I’d love to see influence the genre.
A spirited and open-ended action role-player that blends vampire lore with authentic European history, while introducing an impressive new swordplay and magic-based combat system.

The final assessment of our experience with The Blood of Dawnwalker is undoubtedly positive. Aside from a few flaws in the gameplay systems (likely due to the development team's relative immaturity), the game is easily one of the best action RPGs currently available, thanks in part to a masterfully written story and superb worldbuilding. The only disappointment is a few glitches in the navigation systems, which ultimately dilute the sense of immersion in the universe created by Rebel Wolves, but Coen's adventure in this dark fantasy world bodes well for the developers' future.

Playing The Blood of Dawnwalker is like attending a live rock concert: it's often uncomfortable, the music is sloppy, it's incredibly loud, but the energy and passion knock the walls down. There are numerous technical issues, the execution is far from flawless, many mechanics are poorly refined, the animations often leave much to be desired, and there's a widespread shortage of original assets. On the other hand, Rebel Wolves have staked everything on their historical strengths, on their ability to create unique worlds and develop deeply fleshed-out characters, weaving a web of choices and consequences that pays homage to the great role-playing games of the past, finding the perfect setting for an experience of this genre to shine. A competent, courageous experience, tied to unique gameplay, which unfolds its enormous potential within a framework that is certainly not one for grand occasions, at least not in this pre-launch version. Take it or leave it: the heart of true role-playing games beats in Coen's story, but to perceive it you have to lower the little finger of the form.

Don't mistake this for selective amnesia regarding the various flaws addressed by the reviewer: however annoying some of these limitations may have been, they ultimately pale in comparison to the masterful achievements showcased here. Admittedly, the visual presentation sometimes feels anachronistic, and we find some of the major shortcomings of the talented team behind The Witcher 3 (awful inventory, a slight lack of variety in attack patterns and the bestiary, among other things). Despite these drawbacks, they cannot overshadow the incredibly deep and branching narrative presented here, aided by a successful combat system, superb art direction (both visually and in terms of sound design), and a cast of wonderfully endearing characters. The Blood of Dawnwalker is essentially a salutary and completely timely reminder: the key to any game's success is, above all, to embrace its own identity.

The Blood of Dawnwalker was a very engaging experience during the 18 hours it took me to reach the credits—though it would take much longer if you were to use all the available days and complete more missions. Its strong narrative component helps make the combat challenges feel less tedious.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a compelling action RPG with solid directional combat, engaging time management, and an intriguing duality between human and vampire abilities. Repetitive activities and technical issues hold it back, but Rebel Wolves delivers a promising and enjoyable debut.

The Blood of Dawnwalker stands as a highly promising first step for the Rebel Wolves team. It delivers a deep story, finely crafted characters, and an enjoyable combat system. However, the lenient execution of time pressure, repetitive enemy design, and frustrating technical issues make the game feel like a vampire stepping out before sunset.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is narratively brilliant, but the activities in the Sangora Valley don’t live up to its story and characters. An imperfect but promising debut. Let’s hope it lays the foundations for a great saga.

The Blood of the Dawnwalker is full of good intentions in every respect: the time-management gameplay, the human/vampire duality for the RPG elements, the directional parry system in combat, and the impact of player choices. However, each of these aspects is held back by mediocre execution—whether it’s the overly limited bestiary, the rudimentary writing, or inconsistencies in game design. In its determination to follow in the footsteps of The Witcher 3, the game never truly dared to stray from the beaten path. By focusing too much on its role model's feet instead of fixing its gaze on its own horizon, it often ends up stumbling. Yet I know it will get back up—and hopefully, this time, it will be to forge its own path.
While The Blood of Dawnwalker and its dark fantasy vampire setting is well worth exploring, best wait for a few patches before exploring its vast open world.

The Blood of Dawnwalker offers a role-playing formula that hits the mark in terms of narrative, but falls short when it comes to combat, world-building and polish. Rebel Wolves is a little too ambitious, despite demonstrating that there is tremendous potential in this role-playing universe featuring vampires.

According to Rebel Wolves, The Blood of Dawnwalker is just the first instalment in a planned series. And honestly, that's what it feels like: a starting point. Fans of vampire fiction or choice-driven RPGs should still gel with Dawnwalker based on the strength of its world building, characters, and deliciously dark tones. But you'll need to stomach some of the most serviceable, yet frustratingly stunted gameplay I've encountered in quite some time.

Despite my mechanical gripes, I remained invested in Coen’s story to the end. The final confrontation encapsulated the many decisions and paths I took and had me face their ramifications one after the other. I may have been unfazed by the time mechanic’s pressure, but the limitation did shape my adventure. The Blood of Dawnwalker shows that curating a massive RPG rather than pursuing every single quest holds immense potential. The ending made me realize that having all the time in the world would have prevented inner ambitions to finally come to broad daylight.

The Blood of Dawnwalker has an interesting core, but it throws too many obstacles in your way before you can get to it. Rebel Wolves builds a rich universe with many stories worth discovering, but its clunky mechanics and various issues with its main systems are hard to ignore.

The Blood of Dawnwalker has a brilliant reactive story and some genuinely clever ideas, but its basic combat, familiar open world and underdeveloped vampire fantasy stop it from becoming the game it threatens to be.

user_reviews.author: flowiscontrol
user_reviews.quote: The Blood of Dawnwalker's atmosphere and world are so gripping and immersive, a dark vampire setting that has some of that Witcher dna but more multifaceted. The time mechanic is what's really unique for me: every choice costs real days and when it comes to saving your family, that pressure makes decisions feel weighty in a way most RPGs never manage. The writing/story is fantastic throughout. The day/night combat split is the standout for me, it's so layered, very addictive once it clicks. For a debut from Rebel Wolves, this was impressive, amazing game and experience. If this is where they're starting, it's going to be a great future and can't wait for sequels.

user_reviews.author: Banehammer
user_reviews.quote:
Witcher 3 meets Vampires? Goty right here!

This game is my highlight 2026 already. Gameplay, Combat, Dialog, Graphics, Sound, Writing and Atmosphere are all amazing here!

Plus it does a couple of nice things that nearly no other games did before, like the dynamic and sporadic dialog options, which are super cool.

This game catches you from the first second and it never disappointed me, quite the opposite!

Its fun, challeging, gripping and everything you would expect from a Vampire Open World game that has The Witcher 3 DNA.

There are very few downsides with this game and no deal breakers here. The performance could be a tiny bit better (on regular PS5). Nothing to worry about but rarely it is noticeable. Another thing is that the movement and climbing can sometimes feel a bit clunky but again, nothing really to worry about.

I am playing with the German synch and it is amazing. Great voice actors and overall quality of translation!

If this is the first game of this studio then holy moly…

user_reviews.author: OmniGodEmperor
user_reviews.quote: Score: 10/10 The Blood of Dawnwalker is the vampire RPG the genre has been waiting for and Rebel Wolves delivered something that belongs in the conversation with the best RPGs this generation.Narrative ExcellenceCoen's transformation from human to something far more dangerous is handled with a narrative weight that most RPGs never achieve. The story respects player intelligence and delivers consequences that feel genuinely earned. Vale Sangora is not just a backdrop. It is a living world with history that bleeds into every quest and encounter. The writing understands the difference between dark atmosphere and gratuitous darkness and walks that line with consistent confidence.Gameplay DepthCombat has depth that rewards mastery without being inaccessible to players still learning its systems. The vampire mechanics are not gimmicks layered on top of a standard action RPG framework. They are woven into how you engage with the world at every level. Movement, combat, and traversal all feel architecturally built around what Coen is rather than what the developers wanted to add as features.Character WritingCoen is one of the more compelling protagonists in recent RPG memory. The supporting cast earns their screen time consistently. Nobody feels like filler and the relationships carry genuine stakes that make player decisions feel meaningful beyond their mechanical outcomes.Audio DesignAtmospheric, immersive, and tonally consistent throughout. The sound design understands what kind of world Vale Sangora is and never breaks the tension that the narrative and environment work to establish. Score and ambient design work together rather than competing for attention.Open World ConstructionThe world is rich, dense, and rewards patient exploration with depth that surface play misses entirely. A few systemic elements feel one update away from complete realization but nothing that significantly undermines the overall experience or suggests the foundation is anything less than exceptional.Areas for Post-Launch DevelopmentNew Game Plus is the most significant gap in the current release. A world and combat system this well constructed deserves a proper New Game Plus mode that allows players to carry progression into subsequent playthroughs. This is the one feature request that should be at the top of Rebel Wolves' post-launch priority list.Quality of life refinement in menus, inventory management, and select UI decisions would elevate an already excellent experience. The friction points are minor and nothing breaks the game but they are noticeable to players who engage deeply with RPG systems.Final AssessmentRebel Wolves built something genuinely special with The Blood of Dawnwalker. The care and craft visible across every layer of this game reflects a development team that understood exactly what they were making and refused to compromise that vision. Vale Sangora is one of the most realized open world settings in recent RPG **** the entire Rebel Wolves team: the ambition, execution, and attention to detail in this game are visible and appreciated. This is what the genre looks like when developers trust their vision.10/10. One of the best RPGs this generation. Essential.

user_reviews.author: Drizztein
user_reviews.quote:
At its core, Blood of the Dawnwalker is a game driven by rich narrative, meaningful choices, true replayability, and genuine originality. While it might fall slightly short in pure graphical fidelity or mechanical complexity, those of us who deeply love video games crave unique titles like this over generic releases and endless copy-paste sequels.​

Metacritic scores often feel completely broken, yet unfortunately, too many people let them dictate what they play. When a title lands below an 80 or 90, it instantly deters players, regardless of its actual quality. Games like this are built for a specific audience, and within its intended scope, it excels brilliantly.​

We see this score inflation issue all the time. Look at Crimson Desert, a game I have poured nearly 400 hours into: does it deserve a mid-70s score given everything its world has to offer? Absolutely not. Yet the next annual FIFA iteration will easily score in the high 80s for doing the bare minimum. It simply makes no sense.​

We need to support and celebrate games like this. This is the debut title from a group of developers coming together for the first time, and they have delivered something where all the pieces actually work. Sure, it stumbles in a few minor areas, but it remains a fantastic game through and through, even its combat is genuinely entertaining. Where it truly shines, though, is its storytelling and narrative depth.​

While I am tempted to give it a 10 just to help offset the unfair average, a solid 9/10 is the score it genuinely deserves on its own merits. Do not let the arbitrary numbers fool you; this is a gem worth playing.

user_reviews.author: speedynik
user_reviews.quote:
I'm usually the kind of gamer that completes all available side content before moving on to the main story, and Dawnwalker is the opposite of this. Initially I was rather excited to have a game that would force me into making choices, unfortunately the time economy feels broken. 

Something as simple as destroying some barrels costs 3 time, nearly half a day. Everything costs time, a quick and simple conversation could use up one of your precious time chunks. The problem with the time economy being broken was that it made me feel like there was no point to making choices, and so I just did whatever I stumbled across that looked mildly entertaining.

Most skills also cost time despite also needing you to find books out in the world. Given the broken economy I'd have found it better if perhaps side quest content gave you the opportunity to skip the time costs for skills, a way to showcase your characters practical experience.

Time moves depressingly fast with all the multi time cost activities, it makes the world feel rushed rather than pressured. I understand the developers wanted to cut out activity bloat, but in an open world game it's also what gives a character a sense of place and allows the player to actually get lost in the world. I would have liked more relaxing side activities (non-combat) that didn't cost time to break up the rush and allow you to actually enjoy places like Svartau. Instead of just, run here, kill the guards, complete.

I'm not against the time system as a concept, but I think Dawnwalker could have used some refining.

I enjoyed the narrative. It was exciting to see how all my choices and the people I'd met would have impact, sometimes in the last place I would have expected it and yet it always worked. The game does a great job in allowing you to connect more with the NPC's and their lives, already from the first minutes of the prologue/tutorial area. No easy feat.

Combat is decent, as a personal preference it feels a bit too heavy but the directional parrying is a fun reaction game. It shines especially well during one on one duels but as soon as mobs get involved the camera really gets in the way and it becomes a bit tedious.

Performance wise I had no problems on the PS5. Looks wise, it's not a 10/10 but it is definitely good enough just a tiny bit dated. It would've likely helped if there was a bit more identity to each of the regions, something to visually mix it up a bit more.

It's an enjoyable game that unfortunately shoots itself in the foot on a couple key occasions.
